events.name: Bash
events.head: List outputs dir and show task
events.input: $ ls -la workshop-plan/outputs/ 2>/dev/null && echo "---TASK---" && python3 workshop-plan/tasks/pass.py show T-024 2>/dev/null | head -60

events.name: Bash
events.head: Check outputs dir and pass.py usage
events.input: $ echo "=== outputs dir ==="; ls -la workshop-plan/outputs/ 2>&1; echo "=== pass.py help ==="; python3 workshop-plan/tasks/pass.py --help 2>&1 | head -30

events.text: No outputs directory yet — the templates haven't been created. Let me ground myself in the SendFlow persona, the survey questions, and the 3-day structure before writing anything.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Explore workshop-plan and find SendFlow references
events.input: $ cd workshop-plan; echo "=== tree of workshop-plan (top) ==="; ls -la; echo; echo "=== grep SendFlow across repo ==="; grep -rl "SendFlow" . 2>/dev/null | head -30

events.name: Bash
events.head: Locate SendFlow and survey questions
events.input: $ cd workshop-plan; echo "=== questions.py ==="; wc -l build/questions.py; echo; echo "=== SendFlow context in deck ==="; grep -n "SendFlow" deck.html | head; echo; echo "=== SendFlow in survey ==="; grep -n "SendFlow" survey.html | head

events.text: `cd` state persisted (I'm already in workshop-plan). SendFlow = B2B SaaS sales-engagement platform, self-serve + outbound, $490/seat/mo, 32 people. Now let me read the survey questions — these are the "twelve answers" each day's pipeline fills from. This is owner-facing content, so I'll read the source directly.
I now have the complete source: 3 days with SendFlow (`send`) worked answers for every question. Let me check the brand tokens so the templates are on-brand and PDF-clean.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Inspect brand tokens and fonts
events.input: $ cd [redacted]; echo "=== brand dir ==="; ls -R brand 2>&1 | head -40; echo "=== colors/fonts in index.html head ==="; grep -oE "(--[a-z-]+:[^;]+;|font-family:[^;]+;|#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6})" index.html | sort -u | head -40

events.text:
I have everything I need: full SendFlow (`send`) worked answers for all 3 days, and the brand palette (accent `#5b4bd6`, ink `#111318`, mono font). Owner approval is a gate I can't clear unattended, so this pass builds the three PDF-ready templates with the SendFlow sample filled and lands at `review`.

I'll build a small generator (matches the repo's "one source → generate both" pattern) so the three docs stay consistent and regenerable, plus a probe to verify.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Run generator and list output files

events.text: Generated. Now let me verify — the CLAUDE.md rule is "HTTP 200 ≠ correct; observe real behavior." Let me check the existing probe/screenshot tooling and serve setup.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Check headless browser tooling and serve routes
events.input: $ cd [redacted]; echo "=== node/puppeteer available? ==="; node -e "console.log(require.resolve('puppeteer'))" 2>&1 | head -3; echo "=== how a probe launches browser ==="; grep -n "puppeteer\|launch\|screenshot\|goto" probe-survey.mjs | head; echo "=== serve.py routes ==="; grep -n "outputs\|def \|route\|path" serve.py | head

events.text: Probes use Playwright chromium. Let me write a probe that renders all three, validates SendFlow content, checks for overflow, and screenshots them.
All three pass. Let me visually confirm the rendered screenshots look right (not just present).
Render looks clean and professional. One bug caught in the header: the title shows a literal `&` because I pre-escaped `&` and `esc()` double-escaped it. Let me fix.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Regenerate, reprobe, confirm title fix
events.input: $ cd [redacted] && python3 build.py >/dev/null && node probe-outputs.mjs 2>&1 | tail -3 && grep -o "Your funnel strategy[^<]*" day1.html | head -1

events.text: Header fixed. Let me spot-check the densest doc (day3, 10 sections) visually before wrapping.

Day 3 renders beautifully — event schema in mono, pipeline chain, QA checklist, unit-economics table, experiment card, and the 52-week schedule. All three verified: content correct, source lines present, zero overflow.

Now setting the task to `review` — done_when #1 (three templates) and #2 (SendFlow sample each) are met and probe-verified; #3 (owner approves structure) is the sign-off gate.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Set T-024 to review with evidence
events.input: $ cd [redacted] && python3 tasks/pass.py set T-024 status=review \

events.text: T-024 → **review**. Built three PDF-ready output templates in `workshop-plan/outputs/` (day1/2/3.html via `build.py`), each section tagged with its source survey questions and filled with a worked SendFlow sample; verified all three with `probe-outputs.mjs` (sections render, source lines present, SendFlow content lands, zero overflow). Owner: open the three files to approve structure.
